rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase (rent-controlled units)
rules.requirement:
For rent-controlled units, landlords may raise rent each year by no more than the annual allowable increase published by the Rent Board.

For March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 the allowable increase is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. To calculate it, multiply base rent by .016; for example, $2,000.00 x .016 = $32.00, giving a new base rent of $2,032.00. Prior periods were 1.4% (3/1/2025-2/28/2026) and 1.7% (3/1/2024-2/28/2025).

Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from the rent increase limits. So are tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act and some tenancies where another government agency regulates the rent. These tenancies remain subject to the Ordinance's just-cause eviction rules.

The Rent Board also publishes capital improvement imputed interest rates and uncompensated labor rates for related petitions.

unverifiable_exemptions: Tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
Some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency
coverage.summary: Rent-controlled units under the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt, as are Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies and some government-regulated tenancies. Where the local cap applies, the state cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12) yields to it.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just-cause eviction and relocation payments (S.F. Admin. Code §§ 37.9(a), 37.9A, 37.9C)
rules.requirement:
A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of 17 just causes in § 37.9(a), and the just cause must be the dominant motive. Mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.

The causes are:
- nonpayment, habitual late payment or frequent bounced checks
- failure to cure a substantial breach
- severe or continuing nuisance
- illegal use
- refusal to sign a materially similar renewal
- refusal of lawful access
- unapproved subtenant remaining at the end of the term
- owner or relative move-in
- approved condominium conversion sale
- demolition or permanent removal from housing use
- temporary capital improvement work
- substantial rehabilitation of a building at least 50 years old, where cost is at least 75% of new construction
- Ellis Act withdrawal
- lead remediation
- demolition under a Chapter 56 development agreement
- expired Good Samaritan occupancy, with notice within 60 days
- demolition under Planning Code § 317

Just cause is also required to remove housing services such as parking, storage and laundry. Under § 37.2(r) a landlord may temporarily remove such services for mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work.

Relocation under § 37.9C applies to evictions for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation. The landlord pays a per-tenant amount, capped per unit, plus an additional amount for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children.

Relocation under § 37.9A applies to Ellis Act evictions. The landlord pays a per-tenant amount, capped per unit, plus an additional amount for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant.

All relocation amounts adjust each March 1 and are fixed by the date the eviction notice is served. Temporary capital improvement displacement of less than 20 days is governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9, not § 37.9C.

coverage.summary: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. This includes tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits: units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, and some tenancies with rent regulated by another government agency. The state just-cause rule (Civ. Code § 1946.2) yields to the local ordinance.

rules.exemptions: Ordinance exemptions from the eviction provisions are not stated in the documents. Temporary capital improvement displacement under 20 days is governed by Civ. Code § 1947.9 instead of § 37.9C.

rules.title: San Francisco annual security deposit interest rate
rules.requirement:
The Rent Board publishes an annual interest rate that applies to tenant security deposits. For March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 the rate is 4.2%. Prior periods were 5.0% (3/1/2025-2/28/2026) and 5.2% (3/1/2024-2/28/2025).

The documents give no local deposit cap, return deadline or deduction rules. The state rules in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 apply alongside this rate.

coverage.summary: Coverage is not stated in the documents. The Rent Board publishes the rate for San Francisco residential security deposits, and the state deposit law operates alongside it.

rules.effective_date_note: 2026-03-01 is the start of the current rate period (through 2027-02-28). The rate resets annually; the end of the period is not a sunset. The authorizing law's effective date is not in the documents.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C)
rules.requirement:
The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. An algorithmic device is, for example, a software program that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend the rent for a vacant unit.

A tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action. Per a secondary source, tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Each month of use for each affected dwelling unit may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data; tenant or City Attorney civil action; up to $1,000 per violation, each unit-month a separate violation (per secondary source); effective Oct. 14, 2024

coverage.summary: Residential units in San Francisco. No building or landlord-size limits are stated in the documents. The state Cartwright Act algorithm ban (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729) operates alongside it.
coverage.other_conditions: Covers devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rent or manage occupancy.

rules.effective_date_note: The Rent Board notice gives October 14, 2024. The Morgan Lewis alert says 'effective October 2024', which is consistent. The adoption date is not in the documents.
rules.quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.review_note: The ordinance text is not captured. Penalty amounts and unit-month exposure come only from a secondary law-firm alert. Per that alert, the ordinance is at issue in Gomez v. Greystar Management Services LLC (N.D. Cal.).
rules.source_notes: Official Rent Board news notice (D081). The Morgan Lewis alert of Aug. 21, 2026 (DX06) supplies the penalties.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Each month of use for each affected dwelling unit may constitute a separate violation, and tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
